changes: Bounded cache of 16 compact layouts and a shared numeric arena, with private result copies before generator yields. Retained/incremental LU stays isolated.
Ordinary shared-axis scheduler now resumes pending slices within the render budget, as the realtime preset already did. No change to dt, nonlinear stopping tolerances or publication barrier.
Browser crossover benchmark uses the captured 981/861 mm state, pulsatile blood flow, shared replay code and production frame-budget helper.

cpuBenchmark.note: CPU variability is substantial. Second paired repeat totals are nearly equal; do not claim a reliable 7% steady-state speedup from aggregate values.

browser.scope: Actual full physics solver and production frame-budget helper; lightweight centerline renderer; app idle catch-up and complete fluoroscopy renderer excluded.
browser.mainApp: Loads after scheduler edit; no JavaScript error logs. Long captured state was measured in the dedicated benchmark, not the main UI.

rejectedProbes.name: constant-rows
rejectedProbes.reason: Bookkeeping reduction did not deliver a consistent total CPU gain.

rejectedProbes.name: certified-contacts
rejectedProbes.reason: Existing exact-sample fast path gave only a small gain.

rejectedProbes.name: certified-sample-bounds2
rejectedProbes.reason: Per-sample skipping changed the numerical path slightly and increased tail factorization work; reverted.

rejectedProbes.name: newton64
rejectedProbes.reason: Larger Newton active-set budget did not change factorization counts or improve throughput.

rejectedProbes.name: friction-reuse-narrow
rejectedProbes.reason: Friction assembly reuse did not consistently reduce total CPU time.

rejectedProbes.name: early-predictor
rejectedProbes.reason: Immediate recovery from a failed predicted pose increased total CPU and p95 in both paired repeats. Reference path retained.

limitations: 60 accepted physics steps per second remains unachieved.
Full repository suite was not run; previous known historical failures remain documented in earlier reports.
The sampled CPU benchmark includes cold first steps and variable host load. Browser comparisons at different times are illustrative, not controlled paired performance claims.
nextBottlenecks: Step 99 fails the full-dt initial solve after 252 factorizations, then succeeds in two half steps; investigate failed active-set work without removing numerical fallback.
Typical full-step CPU remains about 33 ms even after allocation reuse. Assembly and active-set linear work still need material reductions.
Full-application replay should be exposed as a UI scenario so the complete renderer/scheduler can be measured without programmatic page-state mutation.
